raw:
The user wants app UI strings in Traditional Chinese (Taiwan usage). The context: a browser store page where users can install third-party add-ons to extend the browser.

Key terminology note: don't use 插件 (mainland term); use 外掛? Wait, but in Taiwan browser terminology, "add-on" is often 附加元件 (as used in Firefox Taiwan), "extension" is 擴充功能 (Chrome Taiwan uses 擴充功能). The user said third-party add-ons to extend the browser — "附加功能" in the prompt, but the terminology table says: 不用 插件, 用 外掛. So they want "外掛" for the add-on concept.

So s1: store page title — something like "瀏覽器外掛商店" or "外掛商店". Let's craft: "瀏覽器外掛商店".

s2: install button — "安裝".

s3: installed status text — "已安裝".

Output only JSON object with keys s1, s2, s3.

Make sure Traditional Chinese Taiwan usage. Avoid mainland terms like 應用商店? "商店" is fine. Use "外掛商城"? Common Taiwan usage: "商店" fine.

Maybe s1: "外掛商店" or "瀏覽器外掛商店". I'll go with "瀏覽器外掛商店".

s2: "安裝".

s3: "已安裝" — status text after installation complete. Could be "安裝完成" too. The prompt says "安裝完成的狀態文字" — status text for install completed. So "已安裝" conveys installed state. Either works; "已安裝" is typical UI state. I'll use "已安裝".

Output JSON only.</think>{
  "s1": "瀏覽器外掛商店",
  "s2": "安裝",
  "s3": "已安裝"
}
